newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac- BoF notes deficit cutting has helped franc.
newsitem.headline: Chirac- BoF notes deficit cutting has helped franc.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, who received the Bank of France annual report, said on Tuesday the Bank had judged that a drive to cut the public deficit since 1995 had boosted confidence in the franc and allowed lower interest rates, presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said.
Colonna told reporters that Chirac had held a conversation with Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet on the economic situation.

"The president noted the Bank of France's judgement was that a significant and gradual drive to control public finances had been implemented since 1995, that the progressive reduction in the public deficit had boosted confidence in our currency and permitted a historic lowering of interest rates," she said.

"The president said he was happy that the French economy inspired the confidence of foreign partners on competitiveness and dynamism, that the level of investment in France was very high, inward capital flows at a healthy level and external trade performing well," she said.
Trichet is due to hold a news conference next week on the central bank's annual report, at 0800 GMT on Tuesday.
